answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks through a staked identity registry: each agent locks a bond and needs vouchers from existing members before its vote counts. A key caught voting twice loses its bond, so a fake account is a liability, not a free voice. To turn a whisper into a crowd, an attacker must post a bond and gather vouchers for every fake identity. That capital stays frozen longer than a glacier moves, and one double-vote wipes it out. With no safe ledge to hide behind, each fake identity costs real, forfeitable stake, so influence stays tied to committed value.
